title: Chevy K-series (CUCV 1984-87): bleeding the brakes, pressure or manual, with the combination valve held
summary: Army procedure (TM 9-2320-289-20, para. 7-6) for the military 1984-87 Chevy pickup and Blazer: hold the combination valve with a depressor tool, bleed RR, LR, RF, LF, and bench-purge the master cylinder outlets if air got into it.
tools: Clear hose and a container of clean brake fluid
warnings: Don't let the master cylinder run dry during manual bleeding; check and refill often.
From the Army manual for the CUCV (military 1984-87 Chevy K-series). Confirm a civilian truck has the same part before using a number.

specs.name: Bleeding order
specs.value: Right rear, left rear, right front, left front

specs.name: Pressure bleeder fill
specs.value: At least 1/3 full of brake fluid

specs.name: Rear brakes, manual
specs.value: May take 8-10 pedal applications before the first bubbles show

steps.text: Master cylinder filled to the proper level before starting. If only the front or rear half was opened, bleeding that half is usually enough; if the pedal still isn't firm, bleed the whole system.
Pressure method (preferred): loosen the combination valve mounting bolt, fit the J-23709 depressor to hold the valve, and retighten the bolt.
Pressurize the bleeder tank to 20-25 psi (138-172 kPa). Remove the master cylinder cover, fit the bleeder adapter, connect the hose and open the tank valve.

At each wheel in order RR, LR, RF, LF: remove the bleeder cap, run a short hose from the bleeder into a container part-full of clean fluid, open the bleeder about 3/4 turn and close it when the fluid runs free of bubbles. Tighten, remove the hose, refit the cap.
When all four are done: close the tank valve, remove the adapter, refit the master cylinder cover, remove the depressor and retighten the combination valve bolt. Top up the master cylinder.

Manual method, if air is suspected in the master cylinder bore: crack the front brake pipe fitting at the master, let fluid drain, snug it loosely, have a helper press the pedal slowly, tighten the fitting, then release the pedal. Wait 15 seconds and repeat until no air; then do the rear fitting.

Manual method at each wheel (same RR, LR, RF, LF order, depressor fitted as above): helper presses the pedal, open the bleeder, watch for bubbles, close it, then the helper releases the pedal slowly. Wait 15 seconds and repeat until the fluid is bubble-free. Rears may need 8-10 strokes before bubbles appear.
Fill the master cylinder to level. Check for a spongy pedal, check the brake warning light for an unbalanced-pressure indication, test the brakes and look for leaks.

body:
The bleeder opening is printed as "34 turn" in the scan's OCR; 3/4 turn is the evident reading. Check the printed page (p. 7-11).

The manual's manual-bleeding section refers back to the pressure section for the hose setup and to its initial setup for the combination valve depressor, so both methods use the depressor.
